chronic inhibition of NO synthesis in the rat leads to a decrease in the renal medullary circulation that is accompanied by sodium and water retention, and hypertension.

chronic administration of L‐NAME to rats decreases renal medullar blood flow, increases blood pressure, causes sodium and volume retention, and increases renal medullary tissue levels of angiotensin II.
chronic inhibition of NO synthesis selectively decreases renal medulla blood flow, causes salt and water retention and causes hypertension.

the role of nitric oxide in the control of the renal medullary circulation.
the study of the renal medullary circulation in health and in the presence of hypertension, with particular reference to the role of NO in its control.
the role of nitric oxide in the regulation of renal medullary hemodynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic inhibition of NO synthase activity causes a reduction in medullary blood pressure, which in turn leads to sodium and water retention, and finally to hypertension.
NO is an important regulator of medullary blood circulation and that its absence causes hypertension.
chronic inhibition of renal medullary NO synthase causes hypertension, and that the mechanism by which this occurs is through a selective impairment of medullary blood circulation.

chronic L‐NAME administration causes a decrease in NO production in the kidney, resulting in an imbalance of the vasoactive factors controlling renal medullary circulation.

chronic inhibition of NO synthesis in the rat causes a selective decrease in the medullary circulation, a reduction in the medullar‐cortical blood flow ratio and a decrease in the medullopapillary osmotic gradient.
